claims.text: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibits a large magnetocaloric and barocaloric response.
The untreated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack under load.
The proposed intervention is warm forging at approximately 750–800 °C to about 30% total strain, followed by a short anneal below the magnetostructural transition.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will produce a dense deformation-twin network.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will produce a fine recrystallized or heterogeneous grain structure.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby resist crack initiation and propagation.
A heterogeneous grain structure redistributes stress through strain-gradient hardening and internal back stresses.
The magnetostructural phase transformation is responsible for the alloy's caloric response.
Keeping the relevant treatment conditions below the magnetostructural transition will prevent the new microstructure from interfering with the caloric phase transformation.
The treatment will significantly increase fracture toughness relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will significantly increase ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain its large magnetocaloric response under the same magnetic field as the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain its large barocaloric response under the same pressure field as the untreated alloy.
The proposed benefits apply near room temperature or within the calibrated caloric operating window, at temperatures below the magnetostructural transition.
The proposed benefits apply under both static and cyclic mechanical loads representative of refrigeration devices.
Failure to obtain more than a 20% increase in fracture toughness and ductility, or a caloric-performance loss greater than 10%, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
